memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "For the entrance to the courtyard, provide a curtain twenty cubits long, of blue, purple and scarlet yarn and finely twisted linen — the work of an embroiderer — with four posts and four bases." - Exodus 27:16 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
The courtyard had a single entrance. Not one on each side, not several scattered around the perimeter — one gate, on the east, marked by an embroidered curtain in blue, purple, and scarlet. Anyone coming to worship came through that one opening.

That single gate carried a clear message. God determines how He is approached; we do not invent our own routes. This was not arbitrary strictness. A holy God making a way for sinful people to draw near is an act of enormous mercy, and the way He provides is the way that actually works. One gate meant one dependable, God-given path in.

Jesus made this personal and unmistakable: "I am the way and the truth and the life. No one comes to the Father except through me" (John 14:6). That claim sounds narrow to modern ears, and in one sense it is — there is one gate. But look at the other side of it: the gate is wide open, and it is open to everyone. No one is turned away for being the wrong sort of person. The exclusivity is not about who may come; it is about how. And the how has been provided at God's own cost.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
Do I truly rest in Christ as the way to God, rather than looking for alternatives?
How can I hold this truth with both conviction and genuine gentleness toward others?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord Jesus, You are the one way to the Father, and that way stands open to me. Thank You for opening it at Your own cost. Help me walk through it with gratitude and humility. Amen.
